current_stack_read: Several services in no particular order, with no pathway between them. The prices in D1 run from £120 for extra sockets to £4,800 for a full rewire, but nothing connects a new customer to the biggest job. The easiest sell sits at £165: as Dan puts it, "EICRs are the easiest sell because the agents legally have to have them — no persuading needed" (D2) — yet that £165 job leads nowhere on the current stack. The best-margin job, the EV charger at £950, floats alone with no natural pathway to it. And the dream job is "big ticket, i can plan a whole week around one" (D3), but there is no rung below it that routes a first-time homeowner toward it. The average job value of £850 (B2) suggests most bookings are still fuse board swaps, EICRs and smaller callouts, not the full rewires Dan wants to fill his diary with. The situation is several offers in no particular order: the demand is real, the work is genuine, but nothing steers the right buyer toward the most valuable job.

recommended_stack.name: Home Safety Check
recommended_stack.rationale: D1 lists the EICR at £165. For the S2 buyer — 1930s semi, vague surveyor warning filed away, a smell she cannot locate — this is the lowest-friction honest first step: Dan comes in, photographs the wiring, and writes up in plain English what is dangerous, what is wrong, and what can honestly wait. D2 confirms it as the easiest sell: "EICRs are the easiest sell because the agents legally have to have them — no persuading needed." For homeowners it also directly answers the S2 objection that the electrician is manufacturing work that is not there, because the written report names what can wait as clearly as it names what cannot. When the report confirms what the surveyor vaguely flagged on the 1930s semi, the Full House Rewire conversation follows without a hard sell.

recommended_stack.name: Full House Rewire
recommended_stack.rationale: D1 prices the full rewire at £4,200 to £4,800; £4,500 is the midpoint of that range ((£4,200 + £4,800) ÷ 2 = £4,500), stated as a fixed price in writing per D4. D3 is direct: "more full rewires. big ticket, i can plan a whole week around one, and the before and after photos of the old wiring win me the next three jobs on that street." With D5 capacity at a stretch, one rewire filling a full week beats five smaller jobs covering the same time. The 6-year workmanship guarantee in writing (D4) turns the price comparison around: the buyer is paying for a certified, documented, guaranteed job — not a verbal estimate from someone who has not seen the house. £4,500 is below ten times B2 (10 × £850 = £8,500).

recommended_stack.name: Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready
recommended_stack.rationale: D1 lists the EV charger supplied and fitted at £950; D2 states "EV chargers are the best margin by a mile." Adding the EV charger to the rewire at a combined fixed price of £5,450 (£4,500 core rewire plus £950 from D1) gives the buyer one booking, one week of disruption, and wiring and charging sorted in a single visit — directly relevant to the couples in their mid-40s described in S2 who are at or approaching EV ownership. For Dan, the EV charger margin makes this rung meaningfully more profitable than the core alone, with no extra capacity required beyond the rewire week already in the diary (D5). £5,450 is below ten times B2 (10 × £850 = £8,500).

lead_offer: Home Safety Check is the right first offer for this buyer profile. The S2 buyer is solution-aware — she has searched, posted in the local Facebook group, and already suspects the wiring is worse than she has been told. The £165 inspection gives her a low-risk way to find out the truth in writing, which directly answers her main objection: is the work genuine or invented? The written report, with its named 'what can honestly wait' section, feels different from the commodity EICR certificate she would get elsewhere. When the report confirms what the surveyor vaguely flagged on the 1930s semi, the Full House Rewire follows naturally.
pricing_moves: Place Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready (£5,450) beside Full House Rewire (£4,500) on every quote and on the website, so the £4,500 reads as the measured choice rather than a large standalone number. Basis: D1 lists both services separately at their own prices; D2 confirms "EV chargers are the best margin by a mile" — the premium rung costs Dan proportionally little extra to add once he is already on site for the rewire week.

Deduct the £165 Home Safety Check fee from the Full House Rewire or Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready if either rewire is booked within 60 days of the written report being issued. This makes the entry offer feel like the first step of one job rather than a separate sunk cost, and commits the buyer to a next decision with a clear deadline. Basis: D1 EICR £165; D2 "EICRs are the easiest sell because the agents legally have to have them — no persuading needed."

Take a deposit of one-quarter of the agreed fixed rewire price on booking, with the balance due on certification day. This secures the diary slot — critical given D5 capacity is a stretch — and spreads the buyer's perceived outlay without changing the total price or squeezing margin. Basis: D1 rewire £4,200–£4,800; D5; B6 gross margin 30–60% means the deposit alone covers materials on the low-margin end of the range.

State two EICR prices on one page: £165 for homeowners and £140 for letting agents on volume, both taken directly from D1. Agents on the contractor list see their rate at once, removing the discount conversation entirely. Homeowners see £165 as the stated price rather than the opening bid of a negotiation. Basis: D1 "£140 for the letting agents on volume."

Name the 'what can honestly wait' section as a written line item on every Home Safety Check quote — a stated deliverable alongside the written report and photographs, not a verbal bonus mentioned on the day. This separates the offer from the commodity EICR certificate that agents treat as a legal checkbox (D2), and extends the habit Dan already operates: as he describes in D4, "i put the guarantee in writing on the quote which seems to surprise people" — putting the scope of the report in writing does the same job for homeowners who suspect the scope is invented.
risk_reversal_options: On the Home Safety Check: if the written report misses a dangerous or potentially dangerous fault that a subsequent inspection by any other Part P registered electrician identifies within 90 days, Dan returns to the property and re-inspects at no charge, then issues a corrected written report. This promises only his own action — returning and reinspecting — and directly answers the S2 objection that buyers sit there quietly wondering whether all of this is actually necessary. Basis: D4 "i put the guarantee in writing on the quote which seems to surprise people"; D5 capacity means the guarantee relies on Dan alone, which this does.

On the Full House Rewire and Full House Rewire with EV Charger Ready: the 6-year workmanship guarantee (D4) is written onto the quote as a named, signed term, and any notifiable work that does not pass its Building Regulations certification inspection is redone by Dan at no extra charge until it is certified and lodged. D4 already states "everything notifiable gets certified and lodged properly" — putting this in writing on the quote converts an existing practice into a visible commitment that justifies the fixed price over any quote that arrives without one. D5 capacity means the guarantee relies on Dan's own return visits, which is already how the business operates.
category_note: The word 'electrician' puts Dan in a line-up with every sole trader within ten miles and invites a straight price comparison. The frame that makes this ladder's prices make sense is 'electrical safety for older houses' — a specialist who visits, photographs everything, and writes up in plain English what is dangerous, what is wrong, and what can honestly wait, then fixes it at a fixed price agreed in writing before anyone touches a ceiling. In that frame, the £165 Home Safety Check is the entry to a serious service, not a bargain certificate. The Full House Rewire is a documented, certified, 6-year-guaranteed fix for a 1930s or 1950s house — not a quote to negotiate down. And the EV charger done in the same week as the rewire is one coherent job on a house that has just had new wiring run through it, not two separate callouts. Buyers who are comparing on price alone are not comparing like for like once this frame is set.
